newsitem.title: USA: Worldwide PC market grew 16 pct in 1996 - report. [CORRECTED 00:12 GMT 28/01]
newsitem.headline: Worldwide PC market grew 16 pct in 1996 - report. [CORRECTED 00:12 GMT 28/01]

text.p: The U.S. and the worldwide personal computer markets slowed to their lowest rates of growth in years in 1996, according to preliminary figures released Monday by International Data Corp.
The technology research firm said worldwide unit shipments rose 16 percent last year, marking the first year since 1991 in which sales did not increase by at least 20 percent.
U.S. shipments rose 15 percent following a very strong 1995, IDC said.
The 1996 fourth quarter was weak worldwide, growing only 11 percent, due mainly to depressed sales in Europe, it said.

Compaq Computer Corp maintained its lead in both the U.S. and the global markets for the third straight year, fending off a challenge from International Business Machines Corp, which gained market share for the first time since 1993, IDC said.
Apple Computer Inc lost market share, while Hewlett-Packard Co made its maiden appearance on the list of the top five PC vendors worldwide.
Worldwide, continued rapid expansion of the PC market in emerging markets will be balanced by unfavorable economic conditions in key countries, IDC said.
"The overall health of the PC market is good, but some areas are suffering due to their sluggish economies," said Eric Lewis, manager of Personal Systems Research for IDC.

The U.S. PC market continued its pattern of slowing, yet many brand name vendors saw healthy increases in consumer PC sales in the 1996 fourth quarter, with Compaq, IBM, Gateway 2000 Inc and others gaining market share, the market researcher said.
New entrants, especially Toshiba Corp and Sony Corp, grabbed a slice of the market.

The brunt of the slowdown was borne by Apple and Packard Bell NEC Inc (corrects from NEC Corp/Packard Bell), which experienced delays bringing out their autumn lines and lost ground to more nimble competitors, IDC said.

While U.S. consumer demand for PCs was somewhat less robust than predicted, business demand was excellent, boosting vendors such as Compaq, IBM, and Dell Computer Corp, which have large stakes in the corporate market.
